assumptions.statement: The 26 Chainlink-interface equity feeds report honestly and advance while their market is open
assumptions.breaks_if: an aggregator freezes/dies — nothing on-chain distinguishes frozen from fresh

assumptions.statement: Each tokenized-equity collateral is worth its oracle price per 18-dec unit
assumptions.breaks_if: a token is obtainable far below the oracle price, or represents a fraction of a share while priced as one ⇒ buy → post → borrow is direct theft of lender USDG

assumptions.statement: The CASHCAT Uniswap TWAP window is long enough to be manipulation-resistant on this chain's liquidity
assumptions.breaks_if: short window + thin pool ⇒ sustained push inflates collateral; bounded by Morpho market isolation (market 5 has ~$5 USDG, so impact should be near zero — verify the bound)

assumptions.statement: DualAggregator picks a source that is safe (not 'the higher' / not a stale fallback)
assumptions.breaks_if: source-selection logic can be steered or falls back without a freshness test

assumptions.statement: The single-EOA curator behaves honestly; the 1-day timelock bounds its power
assumptions.breaks_if: an instant (non-timelocked) power can reallocate the vault into a hostile market

invariants.result: Morpho holds 48,525.483821025 USDG ($48,525.48) — the entire lendable side

invariants.statement: For every market: borrowedUSD <= collateralUSD * LLTV
invariants.evidence: OPEN — my 6-field market() decode gave inconsistent share/asset ratios (supply pair 1e6, borrow pair 1.139e6, impossible for Morpho virtual shares); reconcile before quoting per-market debt

invariants.statement: For every market: the Morpho collateral balance * oracle price equals the tokens' real tradable value
invariants.check: compare oracle price vs on-chain DEX price per collateral token (Uniswap V3 USDG pools via factory.getPool + slot0 + liquidity)
invariants.result: PASS, FULL SWEEP — 26 of 28 collaterals compared (ORCL and COIN have no liquid V3 pool). EVERY one tracks its oracle within 0.90%, and every deviation is on the SAFE side (DEX at or ABOVE the oracle): WETH −0.17%, NVDA −0.06%, AMZN +0.33%, SLV +0.33%, GOOGL +0.04%, CASHCAT +0.21%, SPCX +0.13%, SPY +0.01%, QQQ +0.06%, GME +0.05%, USO +0.04%, MSFT −0.20%, SGOV −0.06%, USAR +0.13%, TSLA +0.06%, META +0.03%, AMD +0.21%, MU +0.24%, PLTR −0.11%, INTC +0.09%, SNDK +0.37%, TSM +0.90%, MSTR +0.69%, CRCL +0.36%, ASML +0.83%, BABA +0.14%. ZERO collaterals are obtainable below their oracle price ⇒ the buy→post→borrow theft path does NOT exist on this deployment
invariants.evidence: TARGETS/longbow/sweep_oracle_vs_dex.sh + sweep2 + /tmp/lb/sweep*.tsv; pools confirmed real (22,142B, liquidity>0) except the two flagged

invariants.statement: Oracle price is non-zero and non-stale enough to liquidate correctly
invariants.check: read Morpho's public source (done); fork test deferred
invariants.result: WITHDRAWN AS A FINDING — the missing staleness/bounds check is Morpho's DOCUMENTED design, not a Longbow defect: the source comments say 'Staleness is not checked because it's assumed that the Chainlink feed keeps its promises on this. The price is not checked to be in the min/max bounds because it's assumed that the Chainlink feed keeps its promises.' The live staleness itself is real (NVDA feed updatedAt 44.1h old while ETH's was current — equities are 24/5), but vanilla deployment of a documented upstream assumption is not reportable. Consequence worth recording for the trust model instead: the min/max guard Morpho declines to make is ALSO effectively absent here (every feed: minAnswer=1, maxAnswer≈9.58e52)
invariants.evidence: morpho-org/morpho-blue-oracles src/morpho-chainlink/libraries/ChainlinkDataFeedLib.sol; cast call minAnswer()/maxAnswer() on 0x4a9aBC75… and the aggregators behind 0x78F3556b…/0x379EC4f7…/0x42a95341…

invariants.statement: No single address can unilaterally change the price of the collateral backing the loan book
invariants.check: owner() on the DualAggregator and on the aggregators behind the proxies
invariants.result: FAILS BY CONCENTRATION — one owner address (0xeE27D5Ae…, 171-byte contract) sits above every feed checked. Inherited from Chainlink's deployment, not chosen by Longbow, but it means the entire collateral side depends on one owner being honest and operationally correct
invariants.evidence: cast call owner() on 0x4a9aBC75…, 0x6091E64e…(ETH agg), 0xC9d16E4f…(NVDA agg), 0x5eaa223c…(SPCX agg)

invariants.statement: All 28 oracles price in the same unit (1e36 * 10^(loanDec-collDec)) — no market can be over-borrowed purely from a scaling error

invariants.result: PASS — SCALE_FACTOR 1e24 == 10**(36+6+8-18-8) for the stock markets; decoded prices sane (WETH 2503.0, NVDA 218.32, SPY 765.35, TSLA 365.95, SLV 58.10, SGOV 101.04)

never_should_happen.statement: An outsider borrows more USDG than their collateral is really worth, and walks
never_should_happen.attempt: compared every big collateral's oracle price against its live Uniswap V3 USDG pool price (the precondition for buy→post→borrow)
never_should_happen.evidence: NVDA DEX $215.68 vs oracle $218.30; SPCX $149.38 vs $149.97; GOOGL $337.65 vs $339.05 — all at or BELOW the oracle, so collateral cannot be obtained cheaply. Coverage: 3 of 25 tokens

never_should_happen.statement: A market prices its collateral off a frozen feed while the real asset has moved
never_should_happen.attempt: Measured freshness of all 30 collateral feeds on the LIVE chain rather than trying to freeze one (an outsider cannot freeze a Chainlink feed). Read each oracle's BASE_FEED_1 latestRoundData().updatedAt and compared against the head timestamp.
never_should_happen.evidence: LIVE RPC sweep (not a fork), block head 2026-09-17 01:38:31 UTC. All 30 withdrawQueue markets read (30/30, no failures). For every market: idToMarketParams -> collateral + oracle, then the oracle's BASE_FEED_1 latestRoundData(). ALL 30 oracles are MorphoChainlinkOracleV2 (BASE_FEED_1 resolves on every one, incl. CASHCAT and ORCL - so the '2 custom' oracles are v2 instances with custom feeds, not custom oracle code). Feed age vs head: 0.0h to 5.5h (GME worst at 5.5h). ZERO feeds older than 24h. No frozen-feed condition exists. NSH-2 NEGATIVE.

never_should_happen.statement: A liquidation is executed at a manipulable or stale price that a third party can steer
never_should_happen.attempt: to run: identify the liquidation trigger price source and try to front-run it

never_should_happen.statement: The single-EOA curator moves vault funds into a hostile/malicious market
never_should_happen.attempt: Impersonated the owner/curator EOA on an anvil fork: setCurator(attacker) [instant, succeeded], setFee(0.5e18) [instant, succeeded], setSupplyQueue([one market]) [instant, succeeded, 28->1], then submitCap + acceptCap immediately [reverted TimelockNotElapsed] and acceptCap after +25h [succeeded].
never_should_happen.evidence: fork block 64972513 (fork/FORK_ATTACK_NSH4.md). BLOCKED on the new-market path: a hostile new market needs submitCap -> 24h -> acceptCap, and acceptCap immediately after submitCap reverts 0x6677a596 = TimelockNotElapsed(); acceptCap succeeds only after evm_increaseTime. Separate guardian 0x67f79ccc... can revokePendingCap inside that window. Not outsider-reachable: every power above needs owner/curator/allocator. Two weakenings recorded (not exploitable today): (1) the 24h timelock is bypassed in effect because setCurator + setFee(50%) + setSupplyQueue are all instant and not guardian-vetoable, so a compromised owner key has immediate role/fee/routing control; (2) withdrawQueueLength=30=MAX_QUEUE_LENGTH with all 30 markets enabled and non-zero cap, so _setCap cannot push another market (MaxQueueLengthExceeded) until one is removed. No drain path reached: H3 was NEGATIVE for every comparable collateral. Impact bounded by this vault holding 8.022515 USDG -> Informational; mechanism reusable at scale -> recommend multisig.

sections.name: Curator powers / instant vs timelocked paths
sections.evidence: fork block 64972513, scripts attack_nsh4.sh + attack_nsh4_part2.sh, full write-up fork/FORK_ATTACK_NSH4.md. owner()==curator()==0x1bf704707e9F3f407EbC9364fDAeD08C39893770 (eth_getCode=0 bytes, bare EOA); timelock()=86400; guardian()=0x67f79ccc...; fee()=1e17 live. INSTANT proven: setCurator(attacker) tx status 1 -> curator() read back as attacker; setFee(0.5e18) tx status 1 and 0.60/0.75/0.90/1.00e18 all revert MaxFeeExceeded so MAX_FEE=50%; setSupplyQueue([idx2]) tx status 1 -> supplyQueueLength 28->1. TIMELOCKED proven: submitCap(1e12) status 1, then acceptCap IMMEDIATELY reverts custom error 0x6677a596 = TimelockNotElapsed() (selector computed locally); after evm_increaseTime 90000 + mine, acceptCap succeeds -> time is the only barrier. Cap DECREASE is instant by design (submitCap branches to _setCap directly when newSupplyCap < supplyCap). Source: vault.sol onlyOwner set for setName/setSymbol/setCurator/setIsAllocator/setSkimRecipient/setFee/setFeeRecipient (no timelock); onlyAllocatorRole setSupplyQueue/updateWithdrawQueue/reallocate.
findings: F-LB-1 (Informational, trust/config): single EOA is both owner and curator; roles, fee (to 50%) and supply routing are all instant and NOT gated by the vault's own 24h timelock, and the guardian cannot veto them — only cap increases and market removals wait.

every borrow, withdraw-health check and liquidation resolves through it
converts a mispriced oracle into realised bad debt for that market's suppliers
